data_description.calendars: Leave this empty for the safest setup. A checked calendar is not activated until the next confirmation. Activating a calendar exposes it in Home Assistant, including creating, updating, and deleting events.

calendars.description: None of the discovered calendars are selected. Continue with no calendars, or choose calendars to consider. Nothing is activated until you confirm the next step. CalDAV Full entity ids end in _full. The same name from Home Assistant's built-in CalDAV integration is a different entity.
calendars.title: Calendars

confirm_activate.description: These calendars will be exposed: {calendars}. Activating them enables creating, updating, and deleting events through Home Assistant.
confirm_activate.title: Confirm calendar activation

confirm_none.description: No calendars will be exposed, and CalDAV Full will not create a calendar entity. This is the safest initial configuration. The integration can still sign in and list calendar names.
confirm_none.title: No calendars activated

data_description.calendars: Clear every calendar to expose nothing. A checked calendar is not saved until the next confirmation. Activating a calendar exposes it in Home Assistant, including creating, updating, and deleting events.

init.description: Choose the calendars to expose. Newly discovered calendars stay unselected. Nothing changes until you confirm the next step. CalDAV Full entity ids end in _full. The same name from Home Assistant's built-in CalDAV integration is a different entity.
init.title: Calendars

data_description.password: For Apple iCloud, turn on two-factor authentication, sign in at https://account.apple.com, open Sign-In and Security, then App-Specific Passwords, and generate a password. Official steps are at https://support.apple.com/en-us/102654.

user.description: Enter the CalDAV server URL, username, and password. An Apple iCloud account needs an app-specific password in this field, not the Apple Account password. Other CalDAV servers use their own password.
